metaDescription: Designing a trust-first investing platform for Muslims across Europe

hero.title: Numu Wealth, Sharia-Compliant Investing
hero.summary: Numu is a mobile investing platform that helps Muslims in Europe build long-term wealth through ethical, Sharia-compliant investing. It combines curated portfolios, guided investing, and goal-based experiences to help users invest with confidence.

blocks.html: Muslims in Europe have limited access to investment products that combine transparent Sharia compliance with the simplicity of modern fintech. Existing platforms often assume financial expertise, making it difficult for new investors to get started with confidence.
Our goal was to define an MVP that balanced user trust, regulatory requirements, and business objectives without adding unnecessary investment complexity.

As Lead Product Designer, I owned the end-to-end experience across onboarding, portfolio management, dashboard design, prototyping, and usability validation, working closely with Product, Engineering, and Compliance.

blocks.title: Validation Metrics
items: Time to first value during onboarding
Task success for funding, transfers, and withdrawals
User confidence after completing key investment journeys

blocks.html: The initial release focused on mid-career professionals investing for retirement and family goals. To maximise learning while limiting implementation complexity, we prioritised:

Advanced capabilities such as hybrid advisory and self-directed trading were deferred because they added complexity without supporting the MVP's primary goal: helping new and mid-experience investors start investing with confidence.

items.goal: Build long-term wealth for retirement and family
items.challenge: Needed transparent, Sharia-compliant investing with clear progress toward financial goals.
Felt overwhelmed by investing and uncertain where to begin.
Expected more advanced investment capabilities and personalized services.

blocks.html: Although users differed in investing experience and financial goals, research revealed four consistent needs: transparent Sharia compliance, simplicity, trustworthy guidance, and investing for long-term life goals rather than short-term trading.

The challenge was balancing those expectations with regulatory requirements and business goals. Every product decision needed to reduce friction without weakening trust while encouraging long-term investing instead of transactional behaviour.

items.finding: Users had to complete too many steps before seeing the value of the product, leading to early drop-off.
items.insight: Introduced two-stage onboarding with early product access, reducing time to value while maintaining compliance.

items.finding: The primary MVP audience valued simplicity and goal-based investing over advanced investment tools.
items.insight: Focus the MVP on curated portfolios, guidance, and goal-based investing.

items.finding: Users expected to move money directly between portfolios, not through an intermediary cash account.
items.insight: Hide intermediary cash movements and make transfers feel direct.

blocks.html: Instead of making users complete the full investment setup before seeing value, onboarding was split into progressive steps. Users can explore potential returns through the investment simulator early, then move through identity verification, account setup, funding, and risk assessment with clear progress and context along the way.

Portfolio creation turns investment decisions into a guided journey rather than asking users to navigate financial products themselves. Risk tolerance, investment themes, and personal goals shape the portfolio, while projected growth and allocation make the recommendation easier to understand before committing.

The dashboard keeps the experience centred on what users are investing for, showing each portfolio as a goal with its own progress, performance, and allocation. Moving money follows the same mental model: users transfer directly between portfolios, while the platform handles the underlying cash and settlement mechanics in the background.

The interactive demo and usability testing validated the core product direction before engineering implementation. Compared with earlier design iterations, participants completed key investment journeys more efficiently and reported greater confidence throughout the experience.

items.label: Average confidence after completing key journeys

blocks.html: The project is now in the engineering integration phase. The design continues to evolve through implementation support, edge-case refinement, and collaboration with engineering as the product moves toward development.

This project reinforced that trust is a product strategy, not a visual outcome. Users valued guidance, transparent Sharia compliance, and goal-based investing over feature breadth, shaping a simpler, more focused MVP.

Close collaboration with engineering and compliance also showed that strong financial products often hide complexity rather than remove capability, helping users focus on their goals instead of internal mechanics.
As the product moves through engineering integration, I continue to support implementation, refine edge cases, and prepare for launch.
